headline: $18.5B EQUINOX-ORLA MERGER WINS FINAL COURT APPROVAL — North America's New No. 2 Gold Producer Begins Trading July 31
snippet: The Supreme Court of British Columbia granted its final order on approximately July 29, 2026, clearing the last regulatory hurdle for the $18.5 billion business combination of Equinox Gold Corp. and Orla Mining Ltd. — the largest merger in Canadian gold mining in years. Under the arrangement, each Orla share converts to one Equinox Gold common share plus US$0.0001 cash, with Orla shares delisted from the TSX and NYSE American on or about July 31. The combined company enters the market as North America's second-largest gold producer by output, with an expected 1.1 million ounces per year across a diversified portfolio of mines in Mexico, Brazil, Canada, and California. Existing Equinox investors retain approximately 67% of the combined company. At $4,100 gold, the new entity enters the market generating cash flows that would have seemed implausible just two years ago — and the scale of this deal signals that senior producers are using high gold prices to consolidate assets ahead of what they expect to be a sustained bull market.

headline: FORTUNA PULLS $109M TRIGGER ON SÉGUÉLA: 30% MORE THROUGHPUT, 200K oz/yr WEST AFRICA FOR A DECADE (TSX/NYSE: FSM)
snippet: Fortuna Mining Corp. (TSX/NYSE: FSM) announced July 30 that its board has approved a $109 million capacity expansion of the Séguéla Gold Mine in Côte d'Ivoire — one of West Africa's newest and most profitable gold operations — increasing processing throughput 30% from 1.75 million to 2.3 million tonnes per annum, boosting gold recovery to 94.5%, and adding the Sunbird underground mine to the ore supply. The expansion is designed to push Séguéla above 200,000 ounces per year for the next decade, with construction beginning H2 2026 and a 2.5-year payback period on the $109 million capital investment funded entirely from Fortuna's approximately $800 million liquidity position — no dilution required. For retail investors tracking mid-tier producers, this is the kind of bolt-on capacity decision that is only possible at $4,000+ gold: the same mine that looked marginal at $1,800 is now self-funding a decade-long production expansion from operating cash flow.

headline: G MINING CLOSES $2.8B G2 GOLDFIELDS DEAL — Tier-1 Guyana Gold Complex Created; G3 Goldfields Spun Out as New Explorer (TSX: GMIN)
snippet: G Mining Ventures Corp. (TSX: GMIN) announced July 29 the completion of its plan of arrangement to acquire all outstanding shares of G2 Goldfields Inc. in a $2.8 billion deal that creates a tier-one gold mining complex in Guyana by combining the adjacent Oko West and Oko-Ghanie deposits — two large-scale permitted gold development projects that will share infrastructure, processing capacity, and mine planning in one of the Western Hemisphere's most prolific but underexplored gold belts. Concurrent with closing, G2 completed a spin-out of G3 Goldfields Inc. as a separate publicly traded exploration company holding the earlier-stage assets, giving G2 shareholders two instruments: 0.212 GMIN shares plus 0.50 G3 shares per G2 share held. The deal is a textbook consolidation of adjacent deposits that the $4,000 gold environment has made economically compelling, and Guyana has emerged as one of the hemisphere's most active gold districts over the past five years.

headline: ALLIED GOLD PIVOT: ZIJIN ACQUISITION COLLAPSES, REPLACED WITH $295M STRATEGIC STAKE — Chinese Major Gets 9.2% at TSX Premium (TSX: AAUC)
snippet: Allied Gold Corporation (TSX: AAUC) and Zijin Gold International announced July 29 that their full acquisition arrangement — which would have seen Zijin acquire 100% of Allied — has been mutually terminated, as both parties concluded conditions could not be met by the July 29 outside date or within any reasonable timeframe thereafter. In its place, Zijin has agreed to a $295 million strategic investment: subscribing for approximately 12.8 million Allied shares at C$32.55 per share — a premium to the TSX market price — giving Zijin a 9.2% stake and ongoing strategic alignment with Allied's West African gold portfolio without triggering a full change of control. Completion is expected around August 10, 2026, pending TSX and NYSE approval. For investors, this is a nuanced outcome: Allied retains independence, Zijin retains gold exposure, and a Chinese strategic investor holds a meaningful minority stake in a multi-mine African gold producer — a structure that has become a recurring template in Sino-Canadian gold deals.

headline: ALAMOS Q2: $594M REVENUE +36%, BUT GUIDANCE CUT 12% ON SEISMIC EVENT AT YOUNG-DAVIDSON — Island Gold District Hits Record (TSX/NYSE: AGI)
snippet: Alamos Gold (TSX/NYSE: AGI) reported Q2 2026 results July 29 that underscore both the opportunity and the operating risk in the current gold environment: revenue of $594.1 million rose 36% year-over-year and free cash flow hit $143.5 million, driven by a record quarter at the Island Gold District (67,500 oz, record underground mining and milling rates), but the company simultaneously cut full-year 2026 production guidance by 12% and raised cost guidance 18% after a seismic event at the Young-Davidson mine in Northern Ontario disrupted operations. Full-year guidance now stands at 510,000–560,000 oz with AISC of $1,775–$1,875 per oz — implying $2,200+ per-ounce margins at current gold prices, still exceptional — but a reminder that mine-level disruptions can clip expected output even in the strongest gold market in history. Net earnings reached $270.4 million ($0.64/share, beating consensus by 11%).

headline: FIREFLY GREEN BAY: 42m AT 6.1% CuEq INCLUDING 9.8m AT 16.5% — ASX200 Copper-Gold Restart PEA Due August (ASX/TSX: FFM)
snippet: FireFly Metals Ltd. (ASX/TSX: FFM) released its Q2 2026 Quarterly Activities Report on July 30, confirming outstanding underground drill results from its six-rig campaign at the Green Bay Copper-Gold Project in Newfoundland and Labrador — the restart of a historic high-grade VMS mine that was among North America's top copper producers in its prior operating life. Quarter highlights include 42.0 metres grading 6.1% copper equivalent (including 9.8m at 16.5% CuEq) and a separate intersection of 51.5m at 4.9% CuEq from the exceptionally high-grade Core Zone. The current MRE stands at 50.4Mt at 2.0% CuEq M&I; infill drilling is designed to capture the high-grade core in an updated resource feeding a PEA/Scoping Study for an upscaled restart — now targeted for August 2026. FireFly's recent promotion to the S&P/ASX 200 Index reflects its growing institutional following as one of the few large-scale high-grade copper-gold projects in a stable jurisdiction, and these Q2 results confirm the grades that drove that recognition.

headline: HAMILTON: GOLD STOCKS HIT 2.8-YEAR OVERSOLD EXTREME — Autumn Rally Could Catapult GDX 20–30% by Late September
snippet: Adam Hamilton's July 30 analysis on GoldSeek argues that gold stocks have just emerged from their most-oversold extreme in 2.8 years — a 36.5% summer drawdown driven by Fed rate-hike fears and geopolitical volatility — and are now entering the historically strongest seasonal window for gold equities: the autumn rally. Hamilton calculates that GDX has averaged a 10.1% autumn gold rally since 2001 and typically amplifies the underlying metal move by 2x to 3x, setting up a 20–30% GDX gain if gold stages a conservative 10% autumn rally. The additional catalyst: gold miners are about to report what Hamilton expects to be their second-best quarterly results on record, with record margins at $4,000+ gold driving already-low valuations even lower and attracting fresh institutional capital ahead of seasonal strength. The confluence of oversold technicals, seasonal tailwinds, and upcoming earnings beats is the setup Hamilton has historically identified as the highest-probability entry point in the gold stock cycle.

headline: GOLDHAVEN MAGNO BC: SURFACE SAMPLES HIT 55.3 g/t AU — Cassiar District Structural Corridor Confirmed, Drill Permit Pending (CSE: GOH)
snippet: GoldHaven Resources Corp. (CSE: GOH) announced July 30 the results of follow-up metallic screen analyses from surface exploration at its 100%-owned Magno Project in BC's Cassiar District — historically one of the province's most productive gold belts — with best results returning 55.3 g/t gold in surface rock chip samples collected during the 2025 program. These are surface samples, not drill intercepts, but their spatial association with the district-scale structural corridor identified by the company's 2,320 line-km airborne magnetic survey is precisely the targeting evidence required to justify a maiden drill program. The gold mineralization coincides with silver, lead, zinc, copper, tungsten, and indium — a multi-metal association typical of orogenic gold systems in the Cassiar. Drilling is on schedule to commence following receipt of final permits, with the structural corridor now providing clear geometric priorities for first-pass holes.

headline: PAN GLOBAL PROVIDENCIA SPAIN: 80m AT 2.36 g/t NEAR-SURFACE GOLD — Historic Mine Extends Beyond Previous Bounds, Maiden Modern Drill-Ready (TSXV: PGZ)
snippet: Pan Global Resources Inc. (TSXV: PGZ) announced July 30 that new channel sampling at the Providencia target at its Cármenes Project in northern Spain returned 80 continuous metres grading 2.36 g/t gold — extending near-surface gold mineralization well beyond the historical mine workings into a continuous high-grade zone that has not been tested with modern drill equipment. The Cármenes Project sits in the Cantabrian Mountains of northern Spain, a historic gold and base-metal district with established regional infrastructure and a permitting framework that has seen renewed activity as $4,000 gold re-rates European exploration addresses. Spain's relatively streamlined mining permit pathway compared to other European jurisdictions makes Cármenes an underappreciated addition to the watchlist for retail investors seeking TSX-listed near-surface gold projects outside Canada and Australia.

headline: USAR VS. FREEPORT: MOTLEY FOOL PICKS A WINNER AS RARE EARTH SECTOR COOLS FROM 81% H1 SURGE (USAR, FCX)
snippet: A July 30 Motley Fool analysis pits USA Rare Earth Inc. (NASDAQ: USAR) against Freeport-McMoRan (NYSE: FCX) as two divergent ways to play the critical minerals supercycle — one a pre-production rare earth developer whose stock ran to $43.98 before retreating to the $12–14 range, the other a cash-generating copper and gold giant. The piece evaluates USAR against the backdrop of a CEO transition (Barbara Humpton retiring October 1; Thras Moraitis taking over), a reduced analyst price target (Roth Capital: $40 → $30, Buy maintained), and China's ongoing heavy rare earth export restrictions — the geopolitical tailwind USAR's Round Top Mountain facility is positioned to capture. For retail investors who rode or missed the 81% rare earth sector H1 2026 surge, this buy/sell comparison cuts through sector-wide noise with specific operational benchmarks to determine which company has the better risk/reward from current prices.
